# Results — Study 454 (Three-Outside-Up / Three-Outside-Down)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a bullish
engulfing candle, confirmed by a third bar closing still higher, forecasts a continuation: go
long the three-outside-up** — encoded as a mechanical rule. The engulfing is bars (t-2, t-1); the
confirming bar is t; everything is known by the close of t (no future bars); a long is entered at
the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **428** mechanical three-outside-up entries pooled across the 5 tapes |
| Timing / costs | pattern read on the close of *t* (the confirming bar); enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per entry |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument pattern study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — three-outside-up vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch pattern-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = pattern − random.

| horizon | n | three-outside | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (patt−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 427 | +19.2 bps | 56% | +1.57 | +18.6 bps | **+0.6 bps** | +17.2 bps | +0.04 | 0.972 |
| 10-day | 427 | +34.0 bps | 62% | +2.06 | +27.0 bps | **+7.0 bps** | +32.0 bps | +0.31 | 0.756 |
| 20-day | 427 | +107.5 bps | 67% | +3.93 | +43.1 bps | **+64.3 bps** | +105.5 bps | +1.82 | 0.069 |
| 60-day | 421 | +196.0 bps | 67% | +3.45 | +180.4 bps | **+15.5 bps** | +194.0 bps | +0.27 | 0.790 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks strong (**+3.93** at 20 days,
**+3.45** at 60) — but that is **mostly beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the three-outside-up never
clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar: the closest call is 20 days (Δ = +64.3 bps, Welch *t* = +1.82,
*p* = 0.069), which falls back to noise at 5, 10 and 60 days (Welch *t* = +0.04 / +0.31 / +0.27).
The pattern does not forecast at the desk's threshold.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the apparent edge is concentrated, not coherent

| ticker | entries | three-outside | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (patt−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 91 | +29.5 bps | +0.54 | +26.7 bps | **+2.9 bps** |
| QQQ | 98 | +102.4 bps | +1.58 | +48.5 bps | **+54.0 bps** |
| IWM | 84 | +106.7 bps | +1.54 | +52.9 bps | **+53.8 bps** |
| DIA | 92 | +123.3 bps | +3.15 | +19.6 bps | **+103.7 bps** |
| GLD | 63 | +204.4 bps | +3.26 | +79.8 bps | **+124.6 bps** |

The 20-day delta is positive in all five names, but the broad tape (**SPY**, +2.9 bps) is
essentially flat — the pooled delta is carried by GLD and DIA on small samples (63 and 92
entries). No single-ticker one-sample *t* clears 2 except DIA/GLD, where it is again drift on a
thin count. Not the coherent, cross-sectional edge a real signal would show.

## Confirmation placebo — the third bar is not load-bearing

The decisive "does the confirmation matter?" test: take the set of **all bullish engulfing**
bars (the marginal of "an engulf happened") and pick a random size-matched subset, ignoring
whether the third bar actually confirmed. If price genuinely respects the *confirmation*, the
real confirmed entries should sit far in the right tail of these confirmation-blind draws.

| test | observed three-outside-up 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY confirmation-shuffle | +29.5 bps | **0.890** | 500 |

**89% of confirmation-blind engulf draws match or beat the real confirmed entries** (*p* = 0.890).
The third bar's "confirmation" carries no information — a bare engulf with no confirmation does
just as well. "Engulf-plus-confirm forecasts" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real continuation

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* multi-day continuation after each confirmed pattern
(knob `edge`), the same three-outside rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape
result is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | three-outside | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no continuation) | 248 | −0.8 bps | 53% | −0.02 |
| **0.60** (real planted continuation) | 221 | +792.1 bps | 75% | **+7.90** |

With no planted continuation the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted
continuation lights up at *t* = +7.90 with a 75% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The three-outside-up does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline at
  the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar: pattern − random = +0.6 / +7.0 / +64.3 / +15.5 bps at 5/10/20/60 days,
  Welch *t* = +0.04 / +0.31 / +1.82 / +0.27 — the best (20-day, *p* = 0.069) falls short and
  evaporates at every other horizon. The big one-sample *t*'s (20-day +3.93, 60-day +3.45) are
  mostly beta — the upward drift of long equity indices.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and costs only deepen the hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply and more fully
  by holding the index; the pattern fires ~85 times per name over 21 years and pays costs on
  each, dominating nothing. No capacity question because there is no edge to scale.
- **"Does engulf-plus-confirm forecast?" — BUSTED.** The confirmation-shuffle placebo leaves the
  result intact (*p* = 0.890): confirmation-blind engulf draws do as well as the confirmed ones,
  so the third bar — the entire premise of the *three*-outside over the bare engulfing — carries
  no forecasting information.
